systemIndex.suffix: estimated system index — reference build is {reference}
systemIndex.weights: Graphics card {gpuIndex}, processor {cpuIndex}. Weights at this resolution: graphics card {gpuWeight}, processor {cpuWeight}. Engine version {modelVersion}. This is not a claim about real frame rates.
systemIndex.chipMeasurement: The graphics index was measured for the {chip} chip; there is no separate measurement for the card you selected. Factory overclocking is not reflected in this number.
systemIndex.margin: Measured deviation: {mean}% on average, {max}% at worst. {method} ({measuredAt})
systemIndex.method: each part's index was compared with the ordering an independent source gives for the same parts

bottleneck.label: Bottleneck:
bottleneck.balanced: Balanced — the processor and graphics card are close in capability.
bottleneck.cpuLimited: Processor limiting — the graphics card is noticeably stronger than the processor, so the card may not be fully used.
bottleneck.gpuLimited: Graphics card limiting — the processor is noticeably stronger than the graphics card, so at this resolution the card may not keep up.
bottleneck.gain: If you moved to the best in the catalog: graphics card +{gpu}, processor +{cpu} index points.

missing.indexTitle: The system index cannot be calculated — this number requires a measurement for both the processor and the graphics card.
missing.needBoth: The system index needs both a processor and a graphics card.
missing.noData: There is no performance data for the selected {category}.
missing.partsStillValid: Your selected parts are valid — the compatibility check is running.
missing.fpsStillShown: The per-game FPS list below is still shown:
missing.fpsStillShownWhy: that list only looks at the graphics card and does not take the processor into account. The two numbers answer different questions.

fps.heading: Per-game FPS
fps.pickGpu: Pick a graphics card for per-game estimates.
fps.coveredGames: {count} games have measurements at this resolution: {list}.
fps.noneAtResolution: There is no measurement at this resolution yet; pick another one.
fps.noDataForResolution: There is no measurement at {resolution} yet. Pick a resolution that has measurement data and the list will appear.
fps.noDataForCard: There is no measurement for this card. Per-game FPS can only be shown for cards with collected measurement data; rather than invent a number, we show none.
fps.gpuOnlyTitle: These numbers reflect the graphics card only.
fps.gpuOnlyBody: They were measured on a test system where the processor was not the limit; the processor you selected does not enter these numbers. In processor-heavy games the real result can fall below this.
fps.cpuBelow: Below the reference; in processor-heavy games the gap will be more pronounced.
fps.cpuEqual: This is the reference processor itself.
fps.cpuLimitedWarning: The system index finds the processor limiting in this build — the numbers below may therefore be optimistic.
fps.noCpuMeasured: You have not selected a processor with measurements yet. The list still appears because it only looks at the graphics card.
fps.measuredTitle: This number was measured, not calculated.
fps.estimateTitle: No measurement; calculated from this card's index. Average error {mean}%.
fps.counts: {measured} games have a directly measured number; in {derived} games this card has no measurement and the value was calculated from its index.
fps.marginNote: Measured error of the calculated values: {mean}% on average, 90% of estimates below {p90}%, worst case {max}%. {method} ({measuredAt})
fps.bandNote: The thresholds (30 / 60 / 120) are widely accepted boundaries — an interpretation, not a measurement; they shift with your display's refresh rate.
fps.method: leave-one-out: each measurement was predicted from the other measurements of the same game, without its own data
